correctness.rationale: Exact overlap classification yields all ambiguity zeros. Odd-order character ratios cannot equal -1. Weyl diagonalization gives the square root of the group order times ambiguity magnitude. Row/column-sum kernel provides an independent nullity count; connectivity of the mixed-coordinate graph proves uniqueness for nonvanishing signals. Full prime-field multiplicities come from uniform linear residues. Independent dense lifting and exhaustive small-group numerical checks agree, but universal correctness is algebraic.

value.rationale: The union of two transverse subgroups is a canonical two-dimensional window. Its rank defect and exact Weyl-basis kernel explain which matrix directions remain unobservable, while the entire full-support nonlinear signal class is nevertheless uniquely determined. The prime-field full singular census supplies exact conditioning and an asymptotic near-completeness law; odd-group invariance is structural rather than a parameter-specific tally.
